items.text: The differences in colour in fig B show how the position of equilibrium changes as the temperature changes.

items.label: text
items.text: In hot water the mixture becomes darker brown.The equilibrium position has shifted to the right to produce moreNO2. Note that thevolumehas becomelargerbecause themixture expands as it getshotter.

items.label: text
items.text: In iced water, the mixture becomes lighter brown. This shows that the equilibrium position has shifted to the left toproduce moreNzO4.Note that the volume has become smaller because thereaction mixture has cooled.

items.label: caption
items.text: Fig C showshow it ispossiblefor thereaction tobe spontaneousin each direction.

items.label: list_item
items.text: figCA graph of entropy against percentage NO2 in a mixture of NzO4 and NO2.

items.label: text
items.text: The entropy of NzO4 is less than the entropy of the equilibrium mixture. The change in entropy from pure NzO4 to the equilibrium mixture is positive, so the change is spontaneous.

items.label: text
items.text: Similarly, the change in entropy from NO2 to the equilibrium mixture is also positive.

items.label: text
items.text: The entropy change for a mixture of the two gases in any proportions moving to the equilibrium mixtureis alsopositive,sosuchchangesarespontaneous.

items.label: text
items.text: Fig C also shows that neithertheforward reaction nor the backward reaction can go to completion, as theentropy changefrom theequilibrium mixture toeitherreactant is negative.

items.label: text
items.text: At equilibrium,the total entropy change is zero and

items.label: text
items.text: Stota[forward reaction]=△Stota [backward reaction]

items.label: text
items.text: The relationshipbetween the total entropy of the reaction and the equilibrium constant is given by

items.label: formula
items.text: ΔS_total = R ln K

items.label: text
items.text: whereK can beK or Kp,and Ris the gas constant.

items.label: text
items.text: Note that this matches with the conclusion that a high value ofK corresponds to a large positive total entropy change.

items.text: USINGTOTALENTROPYCHANGETOCALCULATEANEQUILIBRIUMCONSTANT

items.label: text
items.text: As mentioned above, △Stotal = Rln K.

items.label: text
items.text: Rearranging the equation gives us:

items.label: formula
items.text: ln K = ΔS_total / R

items.label: text
items.text: So:

items.label: formula
items.text: K = e^(ΔS_total/R)
